title: Inconsistent Naming Approach for Merged Schools
what_it_is: Inconsistent Naming Approach for Merged Schools

sections.label: Merged school naming approaches
sections.summary: MOE explains three naming approaches for merging schools, says stakeholders were engaged, and will not revisit announced names.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) why there is inconsistency in the approach adopted in finding an appropriate school name for merging schools depending on whether they are primary, secondary or junior colleges; (b) whether the respective schools' stakeholders, including alumni, staff, parents and pupils, are engaged in the process of naming the merged schools; and (c) whether the Ministry is willing to reconsider the names of merged schools to manage ground sensitivities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: This results in three naming approaches to considering the unique situations of each pair of merging schools: retaining one of the two names, adopting a new name, or having a combination of names.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: The combination of both schools’ names may also be repetitive, for example, North View and Northland Secondary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: Hence, where it is meaningful to do so, MOE has combined the English names of both schools, for example, Loyang View Secondary School, which is a combination of Greenview and Loyang Secondary School.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: On balance, a decision was made to have a combined name to allow the merging JCs to move forward as a combined entity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: MOE worked closely with the schools to take into account the interests of stakeholders, including staff, students, alumni, parents and the School Advisory Committees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: The school leaders engaged stakeholders on various key elements of the merger, such as the programmes and values to be retained, as well as the names.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: We will not revisit names which have been announced.

sections.label: Commemorating merged schools' heritage
sections.summary: Schools will develop heritage corners and work with both schools and alumni to commemorate their history.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The opportunity to celebrate and commemorate the heritage of the schools that are being merged is something that we want to leverage on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Schools will be developing heritage corners, looking at opportunities for students and alumni to become involved in the development of material, whether on display or for reference for future generations of students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I do not think there is a going to be a one-size-fits-all because the historical trajectories of the various schools and the various alumni groups are quite different.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we will work with both schools, both sets of alumni to try to find some way of commemorating the heritage and history of both schools.
